venue.name: Orca Spirit Adventures
venue.description: Orca Spirit Adventures runs three hour whale and wildlife watching tours from two docks in downtown Victoria. Open air boats leave from 950 Wharf Street in the Inner Harbour and semi covered vessels leave from the Coast Victoria Hotel and Marina on Kingston Street, and a certified marine naturalist is on board every tour. The semi covered tours are open to all ages and have washrooms on board, while the open air boats do not take children under 6 or anyone under four feet tall. No school or group rate is published, and all bookings go through an outside ticketing system.
venue.address: 146 Kingston Street, Victoria, British Columbia V8V 1V4, Canada

facility_notes.washrooms: Washrooms are available on all semi-covered vessel tours. Open vessel do not have washroom facilities, so we recommend using the facilities at our Wharf Street location before departure.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our tours are not fully wheelchair accessible. Boarding requires stepping from the dock onto the vessel, which may involve a small gap and some movement depending on water conditions.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Open Vessel Tours at Wharf Street: there are pay parking lots at our Wharf Street location as well as street parking nearby. Semi-Covered Vessel Tours at Kingston Street: there is a parking lot at the corner of Kingston Street and Menzies Street, approximately a 7-minute walk to the dock. RV parking is available at 485 Kingston Street, about a 10-minute walk.

restrictions: Open vessel tours require a minimum height of 4 feet (120 cm).
These tours are not recommended for guests who are pregnant or who have current or previous neck or back injuries.
Personal flotation suits are provided and must be worn throughout the tour.
Guests must check in at least 30 minutes prior to departure.
Late arrivals may forfeit their booking without refund.
venue.hours_notes: We have several departures throughout the day during our season, which runs from April through October. Departure times vary by vessel type and time of year.
venue.seasonal_notes: Summer and winter versions of each tour are sold, at different prices. The site says peak season runs from May through October, with a greater than 95% success rate in spotting whales during that time.
venue.price_year_or_season: Summer season rates as listed on the tour pages. Winter tours are priced separately.

programs.name: Semi-covered vessel whale watching tour
programs.description: A three hour whale and wildlife tour on a semi covered boat with seating, full washrooms and an upper viewing deck, guided by a certified marine naturalist. Prices are per person: $159 for adults 19 and over, $129 for youth 13 to 18, $109 for children 3 to 12, and infants aged 0 to 2 go free. A $4 wildlife conservation fee is listed as included. Hot drinks are free on board and snacks and soft drinks are for sale. The tour leaves from the Coast Victoria Hotel and Marina on Kingston Street, and there is a free shuttle from selected downtown hotels if you ask when you book.
programs.what_children_do: Sit under cover or stand at the rail of an open upper deck for three hours, watching for whales, sea lions and eagles while a naturalist explains what is in the water.
programs.our_note: Three hours on a boat with no way off is a long stretch for little ones, and the washroom on board is the only one they will see. Under threes go free, which makes this the cheaper of their two boats for a group with very young children.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms, seating and shelter are on board and the tour runs three hours from a downtown dock. Their tours are not fully wheelchair accessible and no group or school rate is published, so ask what a group of children would pay.
programs.extra_fees_note: Youth aged 13 to 18 pay $129 and infants aged 0 to 2 are free. A $4 wildlife conservation fee towards salmon restoration in the Salish Sea is listed as included in the tour.
programs.cancellation_note: Guests may cancel or modify their booking up to 24 hours before the scheduled departure time for a full refund or credit. Cancellations, no-shows, late arrivals, or reductions in passenger numbers within 24 hours of departure will be charged the full tour price.
programs.evidence: This tour is wonderful for all ages, especially those looking for a serene experience.

programs.name: Open vessel whale watching tour
programs.description: A three hour whale and wildlife tour on a 12 passenger open air boat leaving from 950 Wharf Street. Full length cruiser suits are provided and must be worn throughout, and wildlife identification kits are handed out. The price is $169 per person for every age band from 6 upwards, and a $4 wildlife conservation fee is listed as included. Children under 6 and anyone under four feet tall cannot go, and there is no washroom on board, so the site suggests using the ones at the Wharf Street dock first.
programs.what_children_do: Zip into a full length cruiser suit, sit in an open boat for three hours in the wind and spray, and watch for whales with a naturalist on board.
programs.our_note: Under sixes cannot go at all and there is no toilet on board, so this one is out for a daycare group. For a school class, everyone pays the same $169 whatever their age.
programs.practical_summary: Three hours outdoors in an open boat with no washroom on board and a four foot height rule, so the group has to be older children. Parking is pay and display at Wharf Street and there is no group rate published.
programs.extra_fees_note: A $4 wildlife conservation fee towards salmon restoration in the Salish Sea is listed as included in the tour.
programs.cancellation_note: Guests may cancel or modify their booking up to 24 hours before the scheduled departure time for a full refund or credit. Cancellations, no-shows, late arrivals, or reductions in passenger numbers within 24 hours of departure will be charged the full tour price.
programs.evidence: Open Vessel Tours require a minimum height of 4 feet (120 cm).

programs.name: Private open vessel charter
programs.description: The whole 12 passenger open air boat booked for one group, with a flexible departure time, for $1,700. The listed price covers 12 people and the booking has to be made by someone aged 19 or over. Everyone on board must be at least 6 years old and four feet tall, cruiser suits are provided, and a naturalist comes along. If the departure time you want is not offered online the site asks you to call the office.
programs.what_children_do: Ride an open boat for three hours in cruiser suits with only their own group aboard, watching for whales while a naturalist points things out.
programs.our_note: At $1,700 for up to 12 people this only works for a small group, and it still shuts out anyone under 6. The flexible departure time is the one thing that makes it easier to fit around a school day.
programs.practical_summary: A three hour open boat trip for up to 12 people at a fixed price, with no washroom on board and a four foot height rule. Departure times are flexible, but nothing about supervision ratios or a school rate is published.
programs.extra_fees_note: A $4 wildlife conservation fee towards salmon restoration in the Salish Sea is listed as included in the tour.
programs.cancellation_note: Guests may cancel or modify their booking up to 24 hours before the scheduled departure time for a full refund or credit.
programs.evidence: This tour is a 3-hour whale watching & wildlife tour on board a 12-passenger open vessel.

gaps: No school rate, student rate or group rate is published anywhere on the site.

Booking runs through an outside ticketing platform rather than the venue's own site, so no booking link is recorded here. The reservations phone number and email on their contact page are the on-site route.
How many children one adult has to supervise is not stated, and there is no free place for accompanying adults.

Whether a group can reserve a whole semi-covered boat, and what that would cost, is not published. The charters page describes groups of up to 150 but gives no price and asks for an enquiry through a form.
Departure times are not published as fixed times. The site says only that times vary by boat and time of year.
Which months each tour runs is not stated on the tour pages. Their questions page says the season runs April through October, yet winter tours are sold as well (unknown).
Capacity for the semi-covered boats is not published. Only the open air boats are described, as 12 passengers.
Nowhere to eat lunch, no wet weather policy and no stroller storage are mentioned.
The answers on their questions page only appear when each question is clicked, so those answers were read in a browser rather than from the plain page text.
No coordinates are published, so the location is pending geocoding. The address recorded is the Kingston Street office and semi-covered dock. Open air tours leave from 950 Wharf Street instead.

values: Coast Victoria Hotel and Marina, 146 Kingston Street
conflicts.note: Their semi-covered tour page gives two different places to meet. The tour details point to the Coast hotel marina on Kingston Street, while the small print further down the same page says to check in at 950 Wharf Street. Their questions page says Kingston Street. Worth confirming when you book, because the two docks are a walk apart.
